title: Ray's New Primary Arithmetic
sourceTitle: Ray's New Primary Arithmetic for Young Learners (Eclectic Educational Series)
author: Joseph Ray
licenseEvidence: Internet Archive scan (raysnewprimarya00raygoog) of the 1877 Van Antwerp, Bragg & Co. / American Book Co. edition; title page reads 'Copyright 1877'; archive.org marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Published before 1930, so public domain in the USA. Not on Project Gutenberg.
description: A classic 1877 primer that builds number sense one small step at a time: counting and writing numbers, then addition, subtraction, multiplication and division tables, then money and measures. Each day starts with real objects like beans, buttons or coins, moves to the short oral exercise in the book, and ends with three practice problems. The full scanned book is free online.
includes: Link to the exact page of the free scanned book for every lesson
Hands-on practice with real objects every day
3 practice problems with answers per lesson

lessons.title: Lesson I: Counting to 10
steps: Count out 1 to 10 buttons, touching each one as you say its number
Point to each row of balls in the book and say the number; write the figures 1–9
Solve the 3 practice problems below, using objects if needed
lessons.notes: Movable objects beat pictures; keep a jar of beans handy all year.

lessons.title: Lesson V: Reading Numbers to 100

lessons.title: Lesson VI: Writing Numbers to 100

Write the book's number lists on a slate or paper

lessons.title: Lesson VII: Oral Exercises: Numbers to 5

units.title: Unit 13: Tables of Money and Measures (Lessons LXXIX–LXXXIX)
